# `WaterBody`

## `origin`
Roughly matches origin of paired entity

## `height`
Sea level
Always matches `bounds.mins.z` & `bounds.maxs.z`

## `bounds`
`mins` & `maxs` (`vec3`)
Snapped to a `node_size` grid

### Storm Point mu2
![apex_water_bodies_bounds](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/8e4794e4-e0a8-40a9-b6f7-f6eb8ec978b3)

## Indices into other lumps
6 ints, looks like `first_X`, `num_X` pairs
~~Haven't found a lump of a length matching the last `first + num`~~
~~Presumably indexes `Indices` & `Vertices`~~

1st pair indexes `WaterBodyCenters`
2nd pair indexes `WaterBodyVertices`
3rd pair indexes `WaterBodyIndices`

### Storm Point mu2
| first 1 | num 1 | first 2 | first 3 | num 2 | num 3 |
| ------: | ----: | ------: | ------: | ----: | ----: |
|       0 |   246 |       0 |       0 |   984 |  1476 |
|     246 |   244 |     984 |    1476 |   976 |  1464 |
|     490 |   216 |    1960 |    2940 |   864 |  1296 |
|     706 |   168 |    2824 |    4236 |   672 |  1008 |
|     874 |   255 |    3496 |    5244 |  1020 |  1530 |
|    1129 |   235 |    4516 |    6774 |   940 |  1410 |
|    1364 |   124 |    5456 |    8184 |   496 |   744 |
|    1488 |   191 |    5952 |    8928 |   764 |  1146 |

## `targetname_hash`
`uint64_t`
@r-ex connected this to `materials/world/ocean_water`
Hashed the same way as `.rpak` assets, but actually for entity `targetname`s

## `uv_scale`
Small float representing the amount to increment a uv tile across the 1K `WaveData` texture
`1024` * `step_size` represents how many pixels across a tile is (might also be some border amount to avoid bleed)

## `node_scale`
Always `1024.0`, the x & y dimension of a tile in the mesh

# `WaveData`
1024x1024 RGBA 32-bit texture
Only the Blue & Green channels of the texture have data, the rest are blank

## Extraction
```python
>>> from PIL import Image
>>> with open("maps/mp_rr_tropic_island_mu2.bsp.0030.bsp_lump", "rb") as raw_file:
...     Image.frombytes("RGBA", (1024, 1024), raw_file.read(), "raw").save("storm_point.wave_data.raw.tga")
```
Alpha channel will need to be inverted / disabled, otherwise the image will appear invisible
If you save as `.png` transparent pixels' colour will be deleted.

## Raw Tilesheets
### Storm Point
![storm_point wave_data](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/8cc640fb-24e9-4ed2-b8cd-1473eb383be2)
### Habitat
![habitat wave_data](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/111a7c92-3561-44b0-aa16-2221c4da2849)

Managed to use these textures as tilesets in Aseprite
Could piece together some patterns, was kinda painful tho

No idea what the gradient is about yet

I presume these tiles get indexed to create textures somewhere

Indices likely start at the bottom left corner
Building a row from tiles as you increment upwards can make some legible shapes
However it quickly falls apart, some tiles might be getting rotated & reused
![wave_data_habitat_tiles](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/a9c25814-9445-444b-8716-189f29b6cb72)

# `WaterBodyVertex`
```python
class WaterBodyVertex(base.Struct):  # LUMP 46 (002E)
    position: vector.vec3
    uv: vector.vec2
    colour: colour.RGBA32
    _format = "5f4b"
```

`colour` is always 100% white or 100% blue
Might act as a mask in the shader

```python
>>> import bsp_tool
>>> bsp = bsp_tool.load_bsp("E:/Mod/ApexLegends/season19/1feb24/maps/mp_rr_tropic_island_mu2.bsp")
>>> from bsp_tool.utils import geometry
>>> model = geometry.Model([bsp.external.water_body_mesh(i) for i in range(4)])
>>> from bsp_tool.extensions.geometry import obj
>>> obj.Obj([model]).save_as("habitat_water_bodies.obj")
```
![wave_data_storm_point_meshes_fixed](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/assets/36507175/f214807a-a397-44eb-924d-0f27090b307e)

Now `.water_body_model`, since we have `origin`
Also trying to get `material` from the entity
Not matching the entity to the `WaterBody` atm tho, just assuming they all use the same material

# `water_body` entity
```python
>>> import bsp_tool
>>> bsp = bsp_tool.load_bsp("E:/Mod/ApexLegends/season19/1feb24/maps/mp_rr_tropic_island_mu2.bsp")
>>> bsp.external.ENTITIES.search(classname="water_body")
[{'surfpropindex': '14',
  'solid': '0',
  'nodesize': '1024',
  'model': 'mdl/dev/editor_ref.rmdl',
  'origin': '-42315.900000000001 16249.9 66',
  'targetname': 'zone_01_water',
  'material': 'world/OceanWater/tropics_ocean_water_01_mu2',
  'height': '-8',
  'classname': 'water_body'},
 ...]  # 8 entries, 1 per WaterBody
 ```
 
 @r-ex found the code which looks up this entity
 Turns out what we thought was an `rpak` asset hash is actually the `targetname`
 
 Can use the entity keys to determine struct member names now

Moving this discussion to the [completed](https://github.com/snake-biscuits/bsp_tool/discussions/categories/completed) category
We still don't 100% understand how the Water Bodies system is rendered, but we understand the structs
